Team maps with leaflet

Saiem Gilani

Source: vignettes/cookbook-leaflet-maps.Rmd
cookbook-leaflet-maps.Rmd
On this page

leaflet draws pannable, zoomable web maps, and sdvplotR’s addSdvLogoMarkers() makes each marker a team logo. The interactive cookbook puts three NFL stadiums on a map and the CFB stadium map every FBS program; the maps here add popups with park data, layer switches, circles sized by a stat, and clustered markers for teams that share a park.

Every coordinate comes from published data, never typed in: the MLB ballparks from the SportsDataverse park table (built from the MLB Stats API’s venues endpoint), and the Big Ten stadiums from CollegeFootballData.com through cfbfastR. The basemaps are Esri’s light gray canvas and OpenStreetMap, which need no key.

library(sdvplotR)
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(leaflet)
library(ggplot2)

season <- 2025
esc <- htmltools::htmlEscape # popup text is HTML: escape names before pasting them in

1. MLB: every ballpark, with its dimensions in the popup

The park table is one row per venue per season, with the capacity, fence distances, roof, elevation and coordinates as of that season. It is a release file on the SportsDataverse data repository (baseballr::load_mlb_park_dimensions() in the development version of baseballr reads the same file). mlb_teams() names each club’s home venue_id, so the join needs no name matching. The park table stores the id as text and mlb_teams() as a number, so both become text first.

parks <- read.csv(
  "https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data/releases/download/mlb_parks/mlb_park_dimensions.csv",
  colClasses = c(venue_id = "character")
) |>
  filter(season == !!season)

clubs <- baseballr::mlb_teams(season = season, sport_ids = 1) |>
  transmute(
    team_id, team = team_abbreviation, name = team_full_name,
    division = sub("^American League", "AL", sub("^National League", "NL", division_name)),
    venue_id = as.character(venue_id),
    spring_venue_id = as.character(spring_venue_id), spring_league = spring_league_name
  )
stopifnot(identical(class(clubs$venue_id), class(parks$venue_id)))

ballparks <- inner_join(clubs, select(parks, -season), by = "venue_id") |>
  mutate(popup = sprintf(
    "<b>%s</b><br>%s<br>Capacity %s<br>Center field %s ft<br>%s roof, %s ft above sea level",
    esc(name), esc(venue_name), format(capacity, big.mark = ","), center_ft, roof_type,
    format(elevation_ft, big.mark = ",")
  ))
stopifnot(nrow(ballparks) == 30, !anyNA(ballparks$latitude))

addSdvLogoMarkers() reads the coordinates and team keys from the map’s data with formulas; label is the hover text and popup opens on a click.

leaflet(ballparks) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldGrayCanvas) |>
  addSdvLogoMarkers(~longitude, ~latitude, ~team, league = "mlb", size = 30, label = ~name, popup = ~popup)

Click Coors Field: 415 feet to center and more than a mile above sea level.

2. MLB: one layer per division

A leaflet group names a set of layers, and addLayersControl() gives each group a checkbox. One addSdvLogoMarkers() call per division, each with its division’s rows passed as data, makes six groups the reader can switch on and off, so the AL East’s five parks can be seen apart from the NL East’s, which share the same stretch of coast.

divisions <- sort(unique(ballparks$division))
division_map <- leaflet() |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldGrayCanvas)
for (d in divisions) {
  division_map <- division_map |>
    addSdvLogoMarkers(
      ~longitude, ~latitude, ~team,
      league = "mlb", size = 30, label = ~name, popup = ~popup, group = d,
      data = filter(ballparks, division == d)
    )
}
division_map |>
  addLayersControl(overlayGroups = divisions, options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)) |>
  hideGroup(setdiff(divisions, c("AL East", "NL East")))

hideGroup() starts the map with two divisions shown; tick the others to add them.

3. MLB: team-colored circles sized by wins

A logo shows where a team plays; a circle can show how it did. addCircleMarkers() draws one circle per row, and its radius (in pixels) and fillColor take a vector one per row. sdv_team_colors() colors each circle with the team’s primary color, and the radius grows with the team’s wins, from baseballr::mlb_standings(). The logos go on top, smaller, so each circle still says whose it is.

wins <- baseballr::mlb_standings(season = season, league_id = "103,104") |>
  transmute(team_id = team_records_team_id, w = team_records_wins, l = team_records_losses)
stopifnot(identical(class(wins$team_id), class(ballparks$team_id)))

ballparks <- inner_join(ballparks, wins, by = "team_id") |>
  mutate(
    color = sdv_team_colors("mlb", team),
    radius = 6 + 30 * (w - min(w)) / (max(w) - min(w)), # 6 px for the fewest wins, 36 for the most
    record = sprintf("%s: %d-%d", name, w, l)
  )

leaflet(ballparks) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldGrayCanvas) |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    ~longitude, ~latitude,
    radius = ~radius, fillColor = ~color, fillOpacity = 0.45,
    color = ~color, weight = 2, opacity = 0.9, label = ~record
  ) |>
  addSdvLogoMarkers(~longitude, ~latitude, ~team, league = "mlb", size = 18, label = ~record)

The circle’s radius is the stat, so compare areas with care: a circle twice as wide covers four times the area. For a strict comparison, scale the radius by the square root of the stat.

4. MLB: spring training, with shared parks clustered

In spring, 30 teams play in 23 parks: 15 in Arizona’s Cactus League and 15 in Florida’s Grapefruit League, and some pairs share a park, so their logos would sit on the same point. clusterOptions = markerClusterOptions() passes through addSdvLogoMarkers() to leaflet’s marker clustering: nearby markers fold into a numbered bubble, and clicking a bubble on a shared park fans its logos out. Each league is a group.

spring_parks <- select(parks, spring_venue_id = venue_id, venue_name, lat = latitude, lon = longitude)
spring <- clubs |>
  inner_join(spring_parks, by = "spring_venue_id") |>
  mutate(label = paste0(name, ": ", venue_name))
stopifnot(nrow(spring) == 30)

spring_map <- leaflet() |>
  addTiles()
for (lg in unique(spring$spring_league)) {
  spring_map <- spring_map |>
    addSdvLogoMarkers(
      ~lon, ~lat, ~team,
      league = "mlb", size = 30, label = ~label, group = lg,
      clusterOptions = markerClusterOptions(maxClusterRadius = 30),
      data = filter(spring, spring_league == lg)
    )
}
spring_map |>
  addLayersControl(overlayGroups = unique(spring$spring_league), options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE))

Zoom into Phoenix or the Gulf Coast to break the clusters apart.

5. College football: the Big Ten, coast to coast

Since 2024 the Big Ten has run from Los Angeles to New Jersey. cfbd_team_info() gives each FBS school’s conference and home stadium coordinates, and its team_id is ESPN’s id, which sdvplotR keys college logos by. The wins come from ESPN’s schedules in cfbfastR’s release files (no key), counted over the regular season and the postseason. Circles sized by wins and colored by team, as in recipe 3, sit under the logos.

CollegeFootballData.com needs a free API key in CFBD_API_KEY (get one at https://collegefootballdata.com/key; see ?cfbfastR::register_cfbd). Without one, this section’s code is shown but not run.

has_key <- nzchar(Sys.getenv("CFBD_API_KEY"))
b1g <- cfbfastR::cfbd_team_info(only_fbs = TRUE, year = season) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(conference == "Big Ten") |>
  transmute(team_id = as.character(team_id), school, venue = venue_name, capacity, lon = longitude, lat = latitude)

games <- cfbfastR::load_espn_cfb_schedules(season) |>
  filter(!is.na(home_score), !is.na(away_score))
records <- bind_rows(
  transmute(games, team_id = as.character(home_id), won = home_score > away_score),
  transmute(games, team_id = as.character(away_id), won = away_score > home_score)
) |>
  group_by(team_id) |>
  summarise(w = sum(won), l = sum(!won), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(identical(class(b1g$team_id), class(records$team_id)))

b1g <- inner_join(b1g, records, by = "team_id") |>
  mutate(
    color = sdv_team_colors("cfb", team_id),
    radius = 6 + 2.2 * w,
    popup = sprintf(
      "<b>%s</b> (%d-%d)<br>%s<br>Capacity %s",
      esc(school), w, l, esc(venue), format(capacity, big.mark = ",")
    )
  )
stopifnot(nrow(b1g) == 18)

leaflet(b1g) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldGrayCanvas) |>
  addCircleMarkers(
    ~lon, ~lat,
    radius = ~radius, fillColor = ~color, fillOpacity = 0.4, color = ~color, weight = 2,
    popup = ~popup
  ) |>
  addSdvLogoMarkers(~lon, ~lat, ~team_id, league = "cfb", size = 24, label = ~school, popup = ~popup)

6. The static version

A leaflet map is HTML. For a print page or a post, draw the logos with ggplot2 at their longitude and latitude over the state outlines from map_data("state") (it needs the maps package), with Canada’s outline for Toronto. coord_quickmap() keeps the map’s proportions.

states <- map_data("state")
canada <- map_data("world", region = "Canada")

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = canada, aes(long, lat, group = group), fill = "grey97", colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_polygon(data = states, aes(long, lat, group = group), fill = "grey97", colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sdv_logos(data = ballparks, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, team = team), league = "mlb", height = 0.05) +
  coord_quickmap(xlim = c(-125, -67), ylim = c(24.5, 49.5)) +
  labs(
    title = paste("Every MLB ballpark,", season),
    caption = "Data: MLB Stats API via the SportsDataverse park table and baseballr | Viz: sdvplotR"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
